conviction_note: Q2 2026 was the best tanker quarter ever recorded and the two-analyst revenue model looks stale, but the print is mechanically a distribution event at this company (each earnings 6-K is the trigger for a 424B3 refreshing an 11.08m-share equity-line resale prospectus that is 170% of the entire non-affiliate float), the fee-earning vessel count stopped growing in Q2, there has been no CFO since 31 May, and the stock has already run 24% in 20 days into it; net a modest negative inside the baseline's 5.13% expected move.

findings.finding: Heidmar's earnings releases are the mechanical trigger for refreshing the resale prospectus covering 11,080,332 shares for B. Riley Principal Capital II: the 424B3 filed 2026-03-24 exists solely to supplement the 20 June 2025 prospectus 'with the information contained in our report on Form 6-K, filed with the SEC on March 24, 2026' - the same day as the Q4 print. The same pattern holds for 2025-08-12 (two 424B3s the day after the 2025-08-11 print), 2025-09-29 (424B3 and 6-K same day) and 2025-11-06, and a POS AM followed the Q1 print by two days. That resale registration was re-declared effective 2026-06-10, so 2026-09-01 is the first print under the refreshed shelf, and 11,080,332 shares is 170% of the company's entire non-affiliate share count.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline records 5 of 6 prints closing down with a 5.13% median reaction but explicitly sets history_usable to 0 and discounts the pattern as possibly describing a dead reporting regime. Nobody has supplied the mechanism, and the mechanism is what makes the pattern forward-looking rather than sample noise. If the market had focused on it there would be visible pre-print weakness in the last five sessions beyond the observed -1.42%, a discount to the sector's Q2 re-rating rather than a 24% 20-day run-up, and the covering analysts would be flagging equity-line dilution rather than modelling flat revenue. No 424B3 or draw disclosure exists yet for Q2, so the size of the refresh is unknown to holders.
findings.independence: Overlaps with the float finding (same 6,498,572 non-affiliate denominator). Independently corroborated by the POS AM's own risk language and by management's Q1 call statement that it kept 'the ELOC live' but had not used it because '$1.27' levels were not 'reflective of the company's valuation' - the stock is now $1.38, above that bar: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-heidmar-maritime-q1-2026-sees-revenue-beat-stock-dips-93CH-4712449

findings.finding: The two-analyst FY2026 revenue forecast of $74.29m implies roughly $18.6m per quarter for Q2-Q4 against Q1 2026 actual of $18.4m - i.e. essentially flat, and below Q4 2025's $25.1m - while the spot rates that drive both of Heidmar's revenue lines rose 47-82% sequentially in Q2 (Frontline realised VLCC $103,500 to $152,700/day, Suezmax $72,400 to $111,500/day, LR2/Aframax $50,700 to $92,400/day, Q1 to Q2 2026), and the five vessels added in March/April 2026 contribute a full quarter for the first time. Heidmar's Q1 revenue was $5.68m trade revenues plus $12.67m voyage and time charter revenues from eight vessels employed on short-term spot/TC voyages versus one a year earlier; the Q2 2025 comparative is $9.6m total revenue and $0.5m adjusted net income.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate data is public but the translation into this company's gross-freight-linked P&L is not: this name has one to two covering analysts who got Q1 exactly backwards (revenue below estimate, EPS beat by roughly 1,000%), demonstrating they do not model the structure. If the gap were priced the FY2026 revenue line would have been revised above Q4 2025's run-rate after the peer prints of the last three weeks, and HMR's 20-day move would look like a tanker-equity re-rating rather than -15% from its own 52-week high. snippet_only on the Frontline TCE figures (globenewswire returned 503 to direct fetch; figures taken from search snippet of that release).
findings.independence: Independently corroborated by SFL's Q2 2026 report (Suezmax spot TCE ~$133,000/day) and Okeanis Eco Tankers Q2 2026 (Suezmax $174,900/day): https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/26/sfl-sfl-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

findings.finding: Heidmar's fee-earning commercially managed fleet was effectively flat through Q2 2026: the 2025 Form 20-F filed 2026-04-30 states 'The Capital vessels compose 25 of the 49 vessels currently managed by Heidmar', while the 2026-07-07 release states the company manages 'around 50 vessels under commercial management and 16 vessels under technical management' - and that is after an acquisition (Q-Shipping B.V., effective 2026-07-01) that the company itself says added nine vessels to the managed fleet. Heidmar has issued no fleet-addition press release since 2026-05-19, the longest such gap since the de-SPAC, against five additions announced for Q1.
findings.why_not_priced: This requires putting two documents filed ten weeks apart side by side; neither figure is a headline and no aggregator carries a vessel-count time series for this name. If it were priced the equity would not have run 24% in 20 days on a platform-growth narrative, and the sell-side FY revenue number would show a decelerating vessel-count assumption rather than a flat one. The count as at 30 June is not public and will be disclosed for the first time tomorrow.
findings.independence: Cross-checked against the 2026-07-07 Q-Shipping release's own fleet counts: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/07/3323069/0/en/Heidmar-Maritime-Holdings-Corp-Expands-Ship-Management-Platform.html

findings.finding: Heidmar has had no Chief Financial Officer since 31 May 2026 - Niki Fotiou ceased in the role and CEO Pankaj Khanna took over 'the finance function' pending a search - and no successor has been announced as of 2026-08-31, three months later. Q2 2026 is therefore the first quarter this company has closed, audited-reviewed and reported without a CFO. Separately, Heidmar has furnished no Form 6-K since 2026-05-28 despite three subsequent material announcements (CFO departure, Nasdaq compliance regained, Q-Shipping acquisition).
findings.why_not_priced: The June departure was press-released and is stale news; what is not priced is the three-month absence of a replacement and the fact that this print is the first one produced without a CFO, which raises the odds of thin disclosure, no quantitative outlook, and a call at which the CEO answers financial questions alone. If holders had focused on it the stock would not have re-rated 24% into the print, and the coverage would carry a governance discount rather than a growth multiple. The vacancy is verifiable only by absence - there is no announcement to aggregate.
findings.independence: Independently confirmed by the SEC filing index, which shows no 6-K after 2026-05-28 and no Form 3 or 6-K appointing a CFO: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002029471.json

findings.finding: Only 6,498,572 of Heidmar's 58,991,997 outstanding shares are held by non-affiliates - an 11.0% float worth about $9.0m at spot - against 20-day average volume of 50,189 shares and short interest of just 127,609 shares. The prospectus states verbatim: 'As of May 20, 2026, we had 58,991,997 Common Shares outstanding, of which 6,498,572 shares were held by non-affiliates of our company.'
findings.why_not_priced: The number sits on an inside page of a post-effective amendment, not on any quote page; every screener reports the 58.99m share count and a float five to nine times the true one. It is not directionally priced because it cannot be - it is a convexity fact, and the baseline has no option chain at all with which to express it, so nothing in the price states a reaction width. Negligible short interest (1.9% of float) also means there is no crowded position to unwind, so a genuine beat has no natural seller.
findings.independence: Short interest figure from a different source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/hmr/statistics/

findings.finding: Three Heidmar directors filed Form 144s to sell 244,862 shares between 2026-06-11 and 2026-07-06 - Andreas Konialidis 113,287 shares ($165,400), Vasileios Loutradis 126,575 shares ($138,699) and Andre Lockhorst 5,000 shares ($5,950) - equal to about 3.8% of the entire non-affiliate float and roughly five sessions of average volume. Both larger sellers were disposing of 104,954-share awards dated 2026-04-01, i.e. registering to sell within ten weeks of the grant. As a foreign private issuer there is no Form 4 to confirm execution.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 144 is an intent-to-sell notice that no insider-trade aggregator reliably surfaces for FPIs because there is no matching Form 4, so the standard insider-transaction feeds show nothing after 2026-04-03. If this had registered with holders, the 24% 20-day run-up would have met visible insider supply in the tape and the coverage would mention it. The relevant scale is against a 6.5m-share float, not the 59m share count everyone screens on.
findings.independence: Overlaps with the float finding (shares sold by affiliates expand the same 6,498,572 non-affiliate base). Second and third 144s are separate filings: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2029471/000091957426003936/primary_doc.xml

findings.finding: Half of Heidmar's fee base sits with one related party that has just been separately capitalised: the 20-F states the Capital vessels are 25 of 49 managed vessels and 'accounted for 37% of our total revenues from the Pools during the year ended December 31, 2025', and Capital Tankers Corp. listed on Euronext Growth Oslo on 2026-03-17 after raising about USD 500m, with a fleet of 30 super-eco crude tankers of which 21 are newbuildings delivering 2026-2028 plus options on 13 more.
findings.why_not_priced: A Euronext Growth Oslo listing is outside the coverage set of anyone following a $81m Nasdaq microcap, and no US aggregator links the two names. The read is two-sided and unpriced in either direction: 21 newbuilds from a counterparty that already supplies 25 of 49 managed vessels is the largest identifiable growth pipeline in Heidmar's model, and equally the largest single point of failure if a now independently funded Capital Tankers internalises commercial management. Neither possibility appears in any Heidmar-facing note. snippet_only on the fleet composition.
findings.independence: Independent of every other finding here; corroborating detail on the newbuild programme and options from a separate source: https://splash247.com/capital-tankers-adds-three-vlcc-newbuilds-from-marinakis-affiliate/

searched_and_found_nothing: Event confirmation - already settled by the sweep; the 2026-08-26 GlobeNewswire release confirms a pre-open 2026-09-01 release with an 08:30 ET call, and I found no contradicting notice, no postponement and no withdrawal
Options market - baseline is correct, there is no listed chain on HMR, so no implied move, no skew and no priced direction to beat

De-SPAC earn-out mark-to-market as a hidden EPS swing factor - chased it because the FY2025 loss included $3.9m of unrealised earn-out charges and the share price rose through Q2; the Q1 2026 6-K reconciliation shows the earnout-shares fair value expense at exactly $0 for Q1 2026 versus $3,917,767 in Q1 2025, so the line is spent and this thesis is dead
Warrant liability - no separate warrant or earn-out liability line is broken out on the Q1 2026 balance sheet, so I could not size any mark-to-market exposure and did not guess

Total debt / covenant headroom - the Q1 2026 release does not disaggregate borrowings and the 20-F excerpt only says covenants exist and could be breached if rates 'materially decline'; no debt figure is obtainable, marked unavailable
Nasdaq listing risk - the April 2026 minimum-bid deficiency was cured on 2026-06-02 and there is no open deficiency; dead angle
Short squeeze setup - short interest is only 127,609 shares (1.9% of float, 2.2 days to cover), so there is no crowded short to squeeze despite the 11% float

Vessel-level Q2 employment data - Heidmar publishes no fleet list on heidmar.com (the /fleet/ page 404s and the homepage gives segments only), so I could not build a vessel-day model and did not fabricate one

Capital Tankers' own Q2 2026 report for a direct read on Heidmar pool TCEs achieved - could not locate the released document; aggregator figures for 'last quarter' were unattributable to a specific quarter and I discarded them
Any HMR-specific news, filing, 8-K/6-K, guidance pre-announcement or trade-press item between 2026-07-07 and 2026-08-26 - a seven-week silence, nothing found
20-F internal control over financial reporting conclusion and any material weakness language - could not extract from the filing or summaries; unresolved, not a finding
Customer/employee-side signals (job postings, Glassdoor, app stores, support forums) - not applicable to a B2B pool manager with roughly a hundred staff
baseline_tension: The baseline is thin by its own admission - no options, no priced direction, and a reaction history it discounts to zero usable events - so its 5.13% expected move is the only thing to beat; my strongest finding cuts directly against that discount by supplying the mechanism (earnings 6-K triggers the 424B3 that refreshes an equity-line resale prospectus sized at 170% of the true float) that makes the 1-of-6 up rate structural rather than noise, and it sits against the 24% 20-day run-up, which I read as the good news from a record sector quarter already being in the price before the print rather than as momentum into it.
